signals.level: VIX ~16.46 close, ~18.17 intraday spike (Sep 10/26)
signals.angle: A vol regime that just showed its first real intraday spike above 18 this cycle — exactly the kind of environment the pool's market-neutral/macro sleeves are built to harvest rather than fear

signals.name: Fitch: private-credit default rate holds at a record 6.0% for a second straight month
signals.reading: Fitch's US Private Credit Default Rate hit a record 6.0% in April 2026 and held at that level in May 2026 — the most recent print found today; a separate Moody's read describes 2026 defaults as 'easing,' a genuine methodology-driven conflict between the two trackers that is not reconciled
signals.level: Fitch private-credit default rate: 6.0% (Apr/26) held at 6.0% (May/26)
signals.angle: A record default rate holding steady rather than reverting — a strong, current contrast point for CCM8752's daily-liquidity structure, though worth noting the Moody's/Fitch divergence if an advisor pushes back

signals.name: Blue Owl's non-traded BDCs show among the most severe redemption pressure yet
signals.reading: Blue Owl's OCIC/OTIC non-traded BDCs saw Q2/26 redemption requests spike to roughly 28.5%/52.9% of NAV respectively — among the highest request rates reported industry-wide — with one unverified source claiming OTIC paid out redemptions at a steep discount ('12 cents on the dollar')
signals.level: OCIC ~28.5%, OTIC ~52.9% of NAV requested (Q2/26)
signals.angle: An escalation beyond the Blackstone/Ares gating pattern already on file — treat the discount-payout claim as unverified, but the request-rate figures alone make a strong illustration of the liquidity mismatch

signals.name: Blackstone's BCRED and Ares' Strategic Income Fund both gated in Q2/26
signals.reading: Blackstone's $77B BCRED, after meeting a record Q1/26 redemption request (7.9%/$3.8B) in full via $400M of firm/executive capital, was gated in Q2/26; Ares' $10.7-11B Strategic Income Fund also gated a second straight quarter, with Q2/26 requests at 14.4% of NAV against a 5% cap, only about a third honored
signals.level: BCRED gated Q2/26 after a record Q1 request; Ares 14.4% requested vs. 5% cap (Q2/26)
signals.angle: The liquidity mismatch at even the largest, most established private-credit vehicles is a durable pattern now spanning multiple quarters and multiple managers — a strong contrast point for daily-liquidity structures like CCM8752

signals.name: Barclays' H2 2026 survey ($8.7T AUM) names market-neutral and macro the two most in-demand strategies
signals.reading: Barclays surveyed 340 investors representing $8.7T in AUM: 43% expect to be net allocators to hedge funds in H2 2026 (the strongest backdrop in years, highest net interest since 2018). Equity Market Neutral is the most sought-after strategy (29% investor interest), Global Macro second (27%), Quant Multi-Strategy third (23%) and Equity Statistical Arbitrage fourth (19%)
signals.level: Market Neutral #1 (29%), Global Macro #2 (27%) investor interest; 43% net allocators, $8.7T surveyed AUM
signals.angle: Third-party validation that CCM8752's two lead sleeves (Picton market-neutral, iAGAM macro) sit in exactly the categories institutional allocators say they want most right now — a strong, current answer to 'why alternatives, why these strategies, why now'

signals.level: ~$19B fund, outperforming 97% of peers over 3yrs; explicit AI-capex-debt rationale for the Asia rotation
signals.angle: A concrete, named, and now better-explained example of how PIMCO is actually trading the AI/geopolitical crosscurrents — strong, specific color for a 'what is our sub-advisor actually doing, and why' conversation

ELITE.compositionNote: Elite Pools & Unified Portfolios continue to draw on PIMCO, Loomis Sayles and iAGAM as sub-advisors. The confirmed structural change at iAGAM remains the Asset Allocation team now led by Tej Rai and Alex Bellefleur following Sébastien Mc Mahon's move to Chief Economist, iA Financial Group (May 19/26) — the claim that this handover extends to 4 segregated funds effective Sep 14/26 has surfaced only once (an advisor-portal snippet) and was not reconfirmed in today's research pass, so treat it as plausible but unverified pending direct confirmation. On the PIMCO side, Bloomberg's Sep 4/26 report is now better understood: manager Emmanuel Sharef's ~$19B fund (outperforming 97% of peers over 3 years) is rotating out of 'Magnificent Seven' US tech and into Asian AI-supply-chain names on the explicit view that AI capex is inflating Big Tech debt burdens while Asia offers more direct 'physical AI buildout' exposure. Loomis Sayles has still not published anything reacting to the latest oil/equity moves; its most recent outlook themes (late-cycle US credit, robust EM high-yield credit metrics) carry no fresh September date. iA Clarington's overall AUM (>$26B, Jul 31/26) and iAGAM's firm-wide AUM ($156B, Jun 30/26, with a newly-found Mar 31/26 asset-class breakdown) were both reconfirmed. This week's live macro test for the fixed-income sub-advisors inside these pools has sharpened further: oil is now above $100/barrel on a US-Iran conflict entering its seventh month, US equities have fallen four straight sessions, and the Canada-US tariff war remains an active, unresolved flashpoint.
